title: A Border for the Cover Revisited
premise: Oscar Villalobos, a financial-crimes investigator who launders reputations as often as they catch criminals, is handed the impossible: a charter flight that landed with every passenger, crew manifest, and radar trace erased mid-flight. Digging in, Oscar discovers the flight carried graduates of a covert training program that manufactures clean identities for the world's worst money — and that their own agency helped build it. To survive, Oscar must burn the network from the inside, trading their last shred of legal legitimacy for a justice that will never be recorded. The novel ends with Oscar erasing themselves as thoroughly as the flight was erased, alive but officially nonexistent, carrying the only surviving copy of the truth.
about_author: Sable Nakamura is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money across borders before turning to fiction. They write from a different city every year, a habit they describe as research they can no longer afford to stop.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. We meet Oscar closing a case no one wants attributed — a bank cleared of sins it clearly committed. The emotional beat is quiet complicity: Oscar is good at making ugly things look lawful, and it's starting to feel like a symptom. A colleague hints at a file that 'doesn't exist yet' waiting on their desk.

chapters.title: Flight 441, Unscheduled
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The impossible arrives: a charter that took off with nineteen souls and landed with no record it ever flew. Oscar pulls the single surviving fragment — a catering invoice. The beat is vertigo; Oscar realizes someone with institutional power erased the sky itself, and that the erasure was sloppy on purpose, like bait.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with a brief intercut of an unnamed passenger's journal. Oscar reconstructs the passenger list from receipts, hotel loyalty points, and a funeral. The journal reveals the passengers were graduates of something called the Cover Program. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose — Oscar recognizes the tradecraft as their own agency's.

chapters.title: What the Training Buys
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following the money, Oscar finds the Cover Program's tuition ledger: dictators' nephews, cartel accountants, one name that makes Oscar's hands go cold — their former mentor, Ines Roldan. Beat: betrayal and self-recognition; the network sells the same clean identity Oscar sells, just without the paperwork theater.

chapters.title: A Meeting Nobody Scheduled
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She summons Oscar, offers them a seat in the Program's successor, and shows them their own file — already drafted, already approved. The beat is seductive horror: Oscar realizes they were never investigating the network; the network was recruiting them, and the vanished flight was their entrance exam.

chapters.title: Nineteen Names
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar tracks the flight's passengers and finds most are dead — used, spent, and cleaned off the books like bad debt. Two are alive, hiding. The beat is grief converted to fuel: Oscar stops trying to survive the system and decides to end it, knowing there's no legal path that doesn't end with them in it.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Oscar and the two survivors, alternating POV. They infiltrate the archive where the Program stores its originals — the true identities beneath every cover. The beat is taut, almost tender: among the files Oscar finds their own birth name, and understands Ines kept it as collateral all along.

chapters.title: Everything Burns in Duplicate
chapters.summary: Climax. Multi-POV. Oscar copies the archive, then torches it — justice outside the law means no one gets their old name back, including the guilty and the dead. Ines corners Oscar in the burning server room and offers the same deal a third time. The beat is fury and clarity; Oscar chooses the fire.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Aftermath: the agency disavows the operation, Ines is officially a retired consultant who never existed, and the flight remains a rumor. Oscar hands the surviving copy of the truth to a journalist, knowing publication will finish their erasure. Beat: costly peace — Oscar finally acts justly and loses everything lawful.

chapters.title: A Border for the Cover
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, final chapter, written in second person for the first time — the voice of someone no longer certain of their own name. Oscar crosses a border with new papers of their own making, the last graduate of a program that no longer exists. The beat is haunting resolution: survival achieved, identity spent, memory the only country left.
